results.summary: sc_6eba02723d4b (family 23553000, 23553000_B_FULL_SCAN 1.ply, AI_GOLD_ACCEPTED, 16 gold lines). Verdict: the gold is correct, and every FN and FP comes from the engine. I mapped the 16 STEP bends (cad_crosscheck_raw/23553000.json) into scan frame using the cad_crosscheck_match pose. Each one lands 1:1 on a distinct gold line within 2.0 deg and 2.0 mm: B1/B6 are the 80 mm flanges, B2-B5 the 4 leg roots, B7/B8 the joggle, B9-B12 the first foot folds, B13-B16 the second foot folds. The cross-sections show gold sitting on the bend apexes. No LABEL_ERROR, FRAME_ISSUE or MATCHER_TOLERANCE cases: the frame is identity, runtime pose fitness 1.0 / rmse 0.78 mm, and best_f1 TPs sit about 1 mm from gold. The part is a bowed 460 mm plate (about 5 mm bow) with 4 legs. The legs are collinear in pairs (7 with 11, 6 with 9), and each foot is a short Z of two folds. Root causes. (1) Active runtime (scores_runtime: 3 lines, TP 0, F1 0.000): the CAD baseline (cad_strategy detector_mesh, native topology UNAVAILABLE) extracted only 4 of the 16 STEP bends. Collinear pairs were collapsed into 133 mm features, and runtime emits lines only for CAD-matched detections. So 9 gold lines get no line at all, even though the scan detector found a 396 mm leg-root line (unmatched detection 'B1', 90.5 deg) that was discarded. The 3 emitted lines are: CAD_B2, extent overrun on B8 (105 mm vs 59 mm, about 22 mm past each plate edge); CAD_B3, merging B9 and B12 across two legs; and CAD_B4, merged and also mislocated 6-11 mm mid-way along the foot segment between the two foot folds. The gated lane (F1 0.211) clips spans and recovers B8 and B9, but CAD_B4 stays 6 mm off. The placeholders lane is identical to runtime: the one NOT_DETECTED placeholder emits nothing. (2) best_f1 (F1 0.435): scan-only a0 produces two 395-404 mm straight lines. Each runs along a whole long plate edge and fuses two collinear leg-root folds with free plate edge. triage_long_lines_profile.png shows bend material only at the leg roots. On the bowed plate the straight line also drifts about 5 mm, which explains the B4 offset. The CAD rescue covers only one leg of each collinear foot-fold pair, and all four second foot folds (B13-B16, 28 mm, about 61 deg) plus the upper joggle fold B7 are missed by every lane. results.summary:
sc_71cf0b216f43 (Gold11 CG84C8FA12D2, family 10839000, 10839000_01_full_scan.ply). The part is a closed rectangular frame of about 312 x 210 x 40 mm with a C-profile: a 40 mm wall, a top and a bottom flange, and two bends per side, so the 8 gold lines are the right bend count. The frame record is identity (residual 0), so this is not a frame problem.

The cross-sections show the scan has both skins, with sheet thickness of about 1.6-2 mm. They also show that 6 of the 8 gold lines are not on their bend:
- Long sides: M05, M06, M07 and M08 were drawn on the flat 40 mm wall face, at a slant. Their offsets from the real bend corner at 20/50/80 % of span are:
  - M05: 6.6 / 11.5 / 16.4 mm
  - M06: 7.4 / 4.5 / 1.6 mm
  - M07: 3.1 / 5.9 / 8.7 mm
  - M08: 6.0 / 6.8 / 7.6 mm
- Short sides: M01 and M02 sit 3.5-5 mm out onto the short 11-12 mm flange, past the end of the bend curve.

Two independent engine paths agree on where the bend corners are: the scan-only A0 lines and the runtime's scan-fitted CAD_B1/B2/B3/B6. That agreement is what shows the gold is the outlier.

The four vertical corners are open seams with a 2-3 mm gap over the full height, not bends. So the 40 mm vertical lines (CAD_B9/B10/B11) are real engine false lines. The cad_guided rescue (best_f1) and the runtime worker both emit them, by fitting two wall planes that meet at a seam.

The runtime gated lane emits no line on the short sides. The worker measured those bends (profile_section, 90.5-91.2 deg, FORMED), but it had only CAD placeholder geometry for them, so the gate dropped them. That is a real ENGINE_MISS.

M03 under runtime_with_placeholders (4.12 mm) is a near-miss caused by where the line is placed. The gold is on the inner skin about 2 mm from the inner corner; the CAD placeholder sits at the outer sharp corner. I classify it as MATCHER_TOLERANCE.

Separately, the gold leaves out the two 35-degree step (joggle) bends on the long-side flanges. The CAD has them and the cross-sections show them. Nothing was scored on them, so they appear in no row.

Estimated rescore with corrected positions only. I did not re-label or re-run anything, so these are estimates:
- best_f1: about 8 TP / 3 FP / 0 FN, F1 about 0.84, up from the reported 0.211.
- runtime gated: about 4 TP / 1 FP / 4 FN, F1 about 0.62, up from the reported 0.000.

The overall finding is that this scan scores low mostly because its gold labels are wrong. It still shows two real engine problems: lines emitted at open corner seams, and the runtime gate dropping short-side bends it had already measured.

results.label: triage:sc_d45186653eed
results.summary:
I found no label errors on sc_d45186653eed (11979003_C, 9 AI-gold lines). All 9 gold lines are physically right; I checked them against slices of points_ds.npz and the independent V10 CAD crosscheck, which has 11 segments, 9 after merging same-plate collinear pieces. The scan scores best_f1 F1 0.125 (TP 1, only B9; FP 6, FN 8) and runtime F1 0.0 (0/5/9). The runtime_gated lane gets 0.143 because it matches B9.

The biggest cause (10 of 14 best_f1 errors, 13 of 19 runtime errors) is ENGINE_SPLIT_OR_MERGE:
- **Window merges:** B2+B3 and B4+B5 are split by a 15.5 mm full-width window into separate plates 5 and 6, but the engine predicts one line across each pair (0.1-0.2deg, under 1.5 mm). Gold covers those lines 100%, yet they cover only 39-52% of the predicted span, below the 0.6 rule, so one correct line becomes 1 FP + 2 FN. Gold and V10 CAD split here. The engine's own compile rule (ENGINE_COMPILE.md 'Windows': one press stroke) merges. This is a convention conflict the owner should decide, not a geometry error.
- **B7/B8:** these are separated by an 11 mm relief with no material near the line. The engine merges them and also runs about 8 mm past each end, so this one is a true engine extent error.

The real engine faults are:
- **ENGINE_WRONG_LOCUS:** the scan-only B1 line is skewed 5.96deg and 5 mm and floats off the surface. The B6 tab bend (33 mm) is stretched to 287 mm. In runtime, CAD_B1 for B9 is 63 mm against 19 mm and runs past the end of the part.
- **ENGINE_FALSE_LINE:** about 254 mm of the B6 stretch lies on a flat flange. CAD_B5 (both lanes) is a 130deg corner seam between end tabs 15 and 18; V10 CAD has no bend there and the labeler correctly rejected that pair.
- **ENGINE_MISS (runtime only):** B1 and B6, because the runtime's 5-bend CAD list omits CAD bends C7-C9 and C2.

Even if window-split pieces were credited, best_f1 would still miss B1, B6 and B7/B8 and keep 2 false lines.

results.label: triage:sc_eaa89c6d1f1f
results.summary:
Scan sc_eaa89c6d1f1f is 40500000 SCAN1: an open 1 mm sheet tray with 4 walls bent off a 184x130 mm base. The AI gold is correct, so none of the misses are LABEL_ERROR. I checked all 9 gold lines against my own cross-sections of points_ds.npz and against CAD V10 (14 segments, all matched to gold). B1-B4 are the base-to-wall bends, which the gold draws merged across the relief and cutout gaps, the same convention the Gold11 humans use. B5 (47.6 mm), B6/B7 (20 mm) and B8/B9 (12 mm) are real 90 deg inward rim tabs. All bends are formed, so the PARTIAL_SCAN_1 stage tag is wrong.

Every FN and FP comes from the engine, through four defects:
1. **Phantom corner bends.** The worker's CAD bend extraction for this part is wrong. It has 8 targets against 14 real CAD segments. 4 of them are vertical box-corner "ROLLED R~14 mm" bends that do not exist. The corners are closed 1 mm butt/welded seams with no overlap flange, and all walls bend off the base. These account for 4 FPs in every lane.
2. **Missing targets.** The CAD target list has no entry for B4, B6 or B7. It merges or mis-sizes the rim tabs into one 137 mm CAD_B8 that is never detected. The runtime even detected B4 itself (unmatched detection, 143 mm, 90.27 deg) but threw it away for lack of a target. As a result the runtime lanes miss 6 of 9 lines.
3. **Rim lines stretched along free edges.** The scan-only a0 lane puts the 20 mm tab bend lines along the whole ~175 mm free top rim of the long walls. The CAD-fusion lane does the same on the x=-92 short wall, with one 134.6 mm line covering both 12 mm tabs. Each tab is on the right locus (0.6-2 mm offset), but the span is 8-11x too long.
4. **Half of B2 dropped.** B2's right collinear segment (x 11..92, 80 mm, clean 90 deg profile) is never reported in best_f1, and the gated runtime clips B2 to its left half. That gives 0.50 gold overlap.

No angle or offset error caused a miss: matched lines are within 0.04-1.4 deg and 0.25-2.2 mm.

**What would fix it:**
- Fix the worker CAD extraction for boxed parts (no corner bends; keep the tab and flange segments).
- Export runtime detections that have no CAD target.
- Bound bend spans to the actual tab support instead of the free-edge extent.

**Matcher note:** gold merges collinear segments, so an engine that reported B2/B3/B4 correctly as separate segments would still fail the 60% span rule. B2 here is partly a convention issue as well as an engine one.

My section renders are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-idantal/db065cf7-f766-4885-b217-ed8d7edd7ade/scratchpad/eaa/ (corners.png, longrim.png, shortrim.png, b2b4.png). Nothing was written to the repo.
